input.question: How do doctors not get sick when they are constantly in close contact with sick people?
input.ground_truth: I'm a doctor. Anesthesiologist, to be specific. The answer is that most people who have a common illness like a cold never actually seek medical attention. If they do, they go to a general practitioner. But GP's are a small subset of doctors. Most people, when they think of "going to the doctor", think of taking kids to a pediatrician, or getting an annual gynecology exam, or something similar, but most doctors don't do that kind of stuff. Most of us are specialists. A small percentage of the population has most of the diseases, and most diseases aren't infectious. (Well, maybe. But we don't have clear causative agents.) I very rarely encounter someone who has an infectious illness in the course of my practice. When I put people to sleep, it's because they have a broken bone, or appendicitis, or gall bladder disease, or some other non-infectious disease process.
